lines: Overall, iron ore tonne-mile trade is still forecast to grow by 4.3% in 2027 and 4.3% in 2028.
Overall, seaborne coal tonne-mile trade is forecast to grow by 1.6% in 2027 and 0.6% in 2028.

As a result, bauxite is expected to remain an important source of tonne-mile demand during the second half of the year and to keep on playing an important role in global dry bulk trade growth, with growth of 3.3% forecast for 2027 and steady volumes for 2028/30.
Looking ahead, grain trade in billion tonne-miles is forecast to grow by 4.2% in 2027 and 2.5% in 2028.
Container trade in billion TEU-miles is forecast to decline by -0.7% in 2027 before moderately increasing by 1.0% in 2028.
Chemical tonne-mile trade is forecast to grow by 5.2% in 2027 and 2.2% in 2028.

desk.headline: Revenue up 77% to $803m, above the $691m estimate; profit $373.9m on record tanker rates; no formal guidance
results: Revenue rose 77% to $803m, well above the $691m estimate, as tanker spot rates soared: VLCCs averaged about $150,000 a day and Suezmaxes about $148,500.
Profit jumped to $373.9m ($1.29 a share) from $17.3m ($0.08), helped by a $100m gain on the sale of two Suezmaxes.
Dry bulk also earned more: Newcastlemaxes averaged $43,001 a day against $29,423 a year ago.
The group will pay $0.65 a share: a $0.21 interim dividend plus $0.44 from share premium, paid on 17 December.
Mineral Europa, the first ammonia-powered dry bulk ship, joined the fleet in October; cash at quarter-end was $68m and the backlog was steady at $3.1bn.

guidance.summary: CMB.TECH gives no profit forecast. It shows Q4 rates booked so far, which are far higher than Q3 for tankers, and three ship sales that will add about $191m of gains in Q4.

points: CEO Alexander Saverys called the tanker market a once-in-a-generation opportunity, but warned the order book of about a third of the fleet could bring heavy deliveries by 2028.
He said more than 20 further ammonia-powered ships are coming; ammonia fuel still costs more than diesel, with parity on green ammonia expected by 2030 at the latest.
The CFO described the dividend, about half of profit, as fully discretionary and said buybacks were not favoured this quarter.
Debt is expected at about $4.4bn by year-end, with 2027 capital spending of about $400m already funded.
Management estimated 2027 free cash flow of about $722m at projected spot rates, and said there is no concrete takeover deal on the table.
